key_insight: A fixed-shape Euler-ensemble theory closely matches freely decaying turbulence data when spectra and structure functions are compared in the appropriate bulk range, with only normalization and scale fitted.
engineering_relevance: This provides a predictive framework for estimating decay laws, spectrum shape, and Reynolds-number trends in decaying turbulence, useful for CFD validation and model calibration.
method: Compare Euler-ensemble predictions against DNS and wind-tunnel measurements for energy spectra and second-order structure functions.
Fit only scale and normalization, then test whether the collapsed spectrum depends solely on instantaneous Reynolds number.
Assess decay exponents and spectral collapse across different initial infrared conditions and cutoff assumptions.
evidence_signal: In the 4096^3 DNS, the extrapolated collapsed spectrum agrees with theory to about 1% in the bulk of the enstrophy range, and wind-tunnel extrapolations match the odd ensemble at large separations.
watch_item: The inferred decay exponents depend on how the infrared spectrum is cut off, so using a finite-flow cutoff as a proxy can be misleading outside the spectral bulk.
paper_title: Number Theory of Decaying Turbulence 3: Comparing with Physical and Numerical Experiments
